partnershipPlan: Two patient partners who stopped reporting during their own treatment co-design the interview guide and review the joint display; triage nurses comment on the alert analysis before it is shared with the rollout committee.
socialListening: No social media listening; the centre's patient feedback forms from 2026 are read for comments on the reporting programme.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I put a nine for the sickness on a Saturday and nobody rang until Tuesday, so why would I keep filling it in?
items.implication: Measure weekend response and link it to later completion.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: My granddaughter set it up, and when she went back to university that was the end of it.
items.implication: Record who needed help and keep a paper or telephone route.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Monday morning there are forty alerts waiting and half are things we already know about.
items.implication: Report nurse time on alerts as a balancing measure.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I did Dad's answers for him, but he never agreed with how I scored his tiredness.
items.implication: Ask who completed the report and treat proxy answers separately.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: The questions come only in English, so our members just stop.
items.implication: Report completion by preferred language and use interpreters in interviews.

summary: Five composite voices on unanswered alerts, device help, alert volume, proxy reporting and language.
